guard: a failure stops the event plane and never the seat: the holder starts the emitter again after a backoff that doubles and is capped, with the first adopt's path and context, reports every failure with the delay, keeps a running emitter and replaces a halted one, and a closed holder never starts again
why: THE DEFECT THIS GUARDS WAS A SEAT EXIT. On a space that requires events, one terminal emitter
failure made every connector stop the seat; for Claude Code that was the MCP server exiting, shown
as a disconnect, and the harness restarted it on the next tool call, so the plane was re-established
anyway, once per keystroke, with a dropped connection each time. The holder now re-establishes the
plane itself, in process, on a backoff.
R1 drops the re-establish timer, so the plane stays down for good and the restart cell reds. R2
retries at a flat delay, so the doubling cell reds. R3 ignores close, so a released holder starts
again and the cancel cell reds. R4 throws a running emitter away on every failure, so the keep cell

mutations.name: R1 a failure is terminal again: no re-establish is scheduled
mutations.note: The old permanent halt, with the delay still reported so only the restart itself is missing.

mutations.name: R2 the delay stops doubling
mutations.note: A flat retry: the plane still comes back, so only the pacing cell can see it.

mutations.name: R3 close no longer cancels a pending re-establish
mutations.note: The timer fires after close: revive clears the failure before `enqueue` refuses the start, so the readable-failure cell is the one that sees it; the start count stays at one either way.

mutations.name: R4 every failure throws the emitter away, running or not
mutations.note: A second start for a refused rebind: two emitters over one write-ahead log, which is the writer-cardinality limit the holder owns.
